title: The dollar only the auctioneer profits from

probes.question: True or false: in the dollar auction, the second-highest bidder also loses the amount they bid.
In the dollar auction, what is the minimum bid for winning the dollar?

image.alt: A 19th-century print of an auctioneer raising his hammer above a crowd of bidders in top hats
image.credit: Charles Maurand (French, 1824-1904) after Honoré Victorin Daumier (French, 1808-1879) printed by François Louis Schmied (Swiss, 1873-1941) published by Jules Meynial (French, 20th century) / Art Institute of Chicago

body.question: An auctioneer sells a dollar bill. The bill goes to the winner, but the second-highest bidder also loses the amount they bid. Once the highest bid reaches one dollar, who profits in the end?
body.reveal: Only the auctioneer. The winner can get a dollar for a mere 5 cents (the minimum bid), but only if no one else enters into the bidding war. Economist Martin Shubik explored the dollar auction to illustrate how a short-sighted approach to rational choice can lead to decisions that are, in the long-run, irrational.
